items.rationale: The solution counts all arrangements of four distinct letters, counts the forbidden immediate ab block as a smaller permutation, and subtracts it. Division rule is inaccurate; permutation counting plus the subtraction rule cover the problem.

Part (a) is an unordered committee selection and needs combination concepts and formula. Part (b) assigns distinct offices without repetition and uses r-permutation counting. The factorial r-permutation form is not needed for the shown product calculation.

The task asks for a general coefficient in a binomial expansion with powers determined by choosing one term from j factors. This is binomial theorem plus the specified-term coefficient method, not Pascal identity or Pascal triangle.

The solution expands a binomial with a negative reciprocal term, solves the exponent equation for j, and returns the coefficient or zero. That matches binomial theorem and specified-term coefficient extraction, not Pascal identity or triangle construction.
The schedule is an ordering of 81 games with repeated indistinguishable opponents, counted by a multinomial coefficient. It is not a ball-box distribution problem.

The unrestricted orders are arrangements of repeated site visits using a multinomial coefficient; the consecutive-X cases are subtracted by treating XX as a block. Ball-box distribution KPs do not model this ordering task.

The problem uses Algorithm 2 to generate all subsets by bit-string order. Existing kp-022 is only lexicographic permutation generation, and the current database has no subset-generation or bit-string subset algorithm KP.

The problem asks for Algorithm 3 listing r-combinations in lexicographic order. Existing combination KPs define and count combinations, but no existing KP covers the lexicographic r-combination generation algorithm.

The proof concerns why Algorithm 3 gives the next lexicographic r-combination. The database has lexicographic permutation generation only, not the r-combination successor algorithm or its correctness argument.
The task computes Cantor digits from permutations. Existing kp-022 covers the next-permutation lexicographic algorithm, but there is no existing Cantor expansion or Cantor digit correspondence KP.
The proof establishes a bijection between permutations and Cantor-expansion digit vectors/integers. No existing KP covers Cantor expansion, Cantor digits, or this bijection.
The problem converts integers through Cantor expansions into permutations. The current lexicographic permutation KP does not cover Cantor-expansion decoding, and no existing KP does.

The requested algorithm generates permutations by enumerating Cantor expansions and decoding them. Existing kp-022 is a different lexicographic next-permutation algorithm, and the database has no Cantor-based generation KP.
